newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Pakistan sees Turkmen gas pipeline start by '98. [CORRECTED 15:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Pakistan sees Turkmen gas pipeline start by '98. [CORRECTED 15:00 GMT]

text.p: Pakistan, terminus of a planned gas export pipeline from Turkmenistan and across troubled Afghanistan, hopes construction on the Unocal project will begin by 1998, Pakistani Secretary at Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources Gulfaraz Ahmad said on Friday.

"By the end of this year, the governments of Pakistan and Turkmenistan plan to start building a gas pipeline from Turkmenistan to Pakistan across Afghanistan with a length of around 1,500 km (938 miles)," he said on television.
"In the nearest time, Islamabad will host a meeting of oil and gas ministers from Turkmenistan and Pakistan to tackle the issues of setting up a consortium and gas prices."
Turkmenistan, Pakistan, U.S. Unocal and Saudi Arabia's Delta Oil signed a protocol last May on the project, which has been repeatedly delayed.

The pipeline, with a projected capacity of 20 billion cubic metres of gas a year, will cost $2 billion and be completed in five years. It will connect southern Turkmenistan's Dovletabad gas field with the town of Multan in central Pakistan.
Pakistan's Ahmad said nothing about the instability in neighboring Afghanistan, ravaged by decades of civil unrest and war.

Pakistan last month became the first state to recognise the government of Afghanistan's new, purist Islamic Taleban militia, which controls most Afghan territory except the north. The gas pipeline would run through the north.
Turkmenistan, which has huge reserves of natural gas but is dependent on Russia's pipeline network for its exports to other ex-Soviet states and to Europe, is also anxious to build the pipeline.
Under the protocol, Unocal and Delta, which will build and operate the pipeline, must formalise by October a consortium to implement the project.
